title: Walk-the-Dog Low Dribble
description: An ultra-low, slow-motion dribble pattern that exaggerates ball control at a walking pace, popular for building a true low dribble before adding speed.

content.objective: Build a genuinely low dribble by walking, not running, through the pattern first.
content.setup: Each player has a ball and walks slowly across half court.
instructions: Walk forward dribbling as low as possible with the right hand only.
Switch to the left hand only for the return trip.
Add a crossover every third step on the next trip across.
Finish with a normal walking pace but keep the same low dribble height.
coachingPoints: Exaggerate how low the dribble is — lower than feels natural.
Keep the knees bent the whole way across.
Only speed up once the height stays consistent.
commonMistakes: Letting the dribble creep up as soon as walking starts.
Standing upright instead of staying in a stance.
Watching the ball instead of keeping the head up.
content.safety: No equipment on the walking path; keep the lane clear.
